paragraphs: Sweetgreen, Inc., a Delaware corporation (together with its subsidiaries, "Sweetgreen," "we,", "us," or the "Company") is a mission-driven, next generation restaurant and lifestyle brand that serves healthy food at scale. Our bold vision is to be as ubiquitous as traditional fast food, but with the transparency and quality that consumers increasingly expect. As of December 28, 2025, we owned and operated 281 restaurants in 24 states and Washington, D.C.

We have designed our menu to be delicious, customizable, and convenient to empower our customers to make healthier choices for both lunch and dinner. We are constantly seeking ways to enhance our menu, all while honoring our food ethos.

Our core menu consists of a curated set of signature items offered year-round across all locations, designed to deliver consistent quality and reflect our food philosophy, supported by a disciplined and scalable supply chain. Guests may also create a custom salad, bowl, or plate from a broad assortment of ingredients and signature dressings, enabling meaningful customization within a standardized ingredient system.

We supplement our core offerings with seasonal and limited-time items that allow us to introduce new flavors and test innovation while maintaining operational consistency. Through our owned digital channels, we also offer exclusive menu items and curated collections that support discovery, personalization, and guest engagement.

Sweetgreen's mission is to build healthier communities by connecting people to real food. Over the past year, our leadership team has evaluated the business and refined our strategic priorities to strengthen execution, enhance the guest experience, and build a more durable financial model. We refer to this framework as the Sweet Growth Transformation Plan which is centered on five strategic priorities:
Drive consistent execution across our restaurants to deliver great food, smooth operations, and reliable guest experiences.
Differentiate through high-quality ingredients and scratch cooking while continuing to evolve the menu in ways that resonate with guests.
Increase customer frequency and average check through targeted digital engagement, personalized messaging, and relevant offers.
Attract new guests by amplifying what makes Sweetgreen distinctive, relevant, and culturally compelling.
Deliver sustainable growth by prioritizing returns, maintaining cost discipline, and allocating capital with rigor.

We have built a differentiated, end-to-end supply chain that culminates in delicious, high-quality food for our customers. Our sourcing and operating standards are guided by the Sweetgreen Way, which is our internal ethos based upon our commitment to ingredient quality, responsible sourcing, and in-house preparation.

We work with a broad network of domestic food partners, including farmers, manufacturers, and distributors. We prioritize ingredients that meet our standards and align with our food philosophy, and we maintain direct relationships with many of our growers and producers. Our supply chain is organized into regional distribution networks, managed in consultation with our lead logistics provider, which promotes consistency, scalability, and operational reliability. As we enter new markets, we seek to leverage existing relationships while maintaining these standards.

At Sweetgreen, we refer to food safety as our "license to operate," and that starts with our food supply. We require our suppliers to provide appropriate food safety certifications as part of the onboarding process. After onboarding, we work with our suppliers to ensure they adhere to our product quality specifications. We also follow a Comprehensive Food Safety Plan ("CFSP"), which includes our Approved Supplier Program, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points Program, guidelines for restaurant design, construction and maintenance, new product commercialization processes, and crisis management. As part of our CFSP, we have a set of "sweet clean standards" for our restaurants, which are guides for operators to ensure our approach to food safety and cleanliness is consistent and scalable across our restaurant fleet. Food safety is an integral element of our field leadership bonus plan; our operators do not receive certain bonuses unless they meet our food safety thresholds for the relevant period. On top of our CFSP sits a system of verification, audits, and monitoring to ensure our food safety is not compromised.

We opened 35 and 25 Net New Restaurants in fiscal years 2025 and 2024, respectively, bringing our total count as of December 28, 2025 to 281 restaurants in 24 states and Washington, D.C. We expect to open fewer new restaurants in 2026 than we did in 2025.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business, Our Brand, and Our Industry
We operate in a highly competitive industry. If we are not able to compete effectively, it could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Severe weather conditions and natural disasters have adversely affected our restaurant sales and results of operations, and climate change may further increase these adverse effects.
We have incurred significant net losses since inception. We expect our net losses to continue in the foreseeable future, and we may not achieve profitability.
We may not persuade customers of the benefits of paying our prices for higher-quality food.
Our future growth depends significantly on our ability to open new restaurants and is subject to many unpredictable factors.
Our long-term success is highly dependent on our ability to effectively identify and secure appropriate sites for new restaurants.
Our expansion into new markets may present increased risks and adversely affect our growth and operating results.
New restaurants, once opened, may not be profitable, and new restaurants may negatively impact sales at our existing restaurants.
Food safety and foodborne illness concerns could have an adverse effect on our business.
If we are not able to hire, train, reward, and retain a qualified workforce, our growth and profitability could be adversely affected.
Increases in labor costs, labor shortages, or unionization efforts could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Changes in food and supply costs or disruptions in the availability or delivery of ingredients and other supplies could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our reliance on third parties could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Failure to manage our growth effectively could harm our business and results of operations.
Changes in commodity and other operating costs, particularly due to climate change, could adversely affect our results of operations.
Failure to maintain our corporate culture could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our marketing strategies and channels will evolve, and our programs may not be successful.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks described below in addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations section and the consolidated financial statements and related notes. If any of the risks and uncertainties described below actually occur or continue to occur, our business, financial condition, and results of operations, and the trading price of our Class A common stock, could be materially and adversely affected. The risks and uncertainties described below are those that we have identified as material but are not the only risks and uncertainties we face. Our business is also subject to general risks and uncertainties that affect many other companies, including, but not limited to, overall economic and industry conditions, and additional risks not currently known to us or that we presently deem immaterial may arise or become material and may negatively impact our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations, or the trading price of our Class A common stock.

We face significant competition from restaurants in the fast-casual dining and traditional fast-food segments of the restaurant industry. These segments compete on factors such as taste, price, food quality and presentation, service, location, and restaurant condition. Our competitors include locally owned restaurants and regional and national chains that offer dine-in, carry-out, delivery, and catering services. Many of our competitors have operated longer and have a more established market presence with substantially greater financial, marketing, personnel, and other resources than we do, and therefore may be better positioned to succeed in the highly competitive restaurant industry. Among our competitors are national and regional fast-casual restaurant chains, restaurants emphasizing clean, real ingredients and health-conscious dining, and traditional quick-service restaurants.

As we continue to expand into new markets and further develop our digital channels, we also face growing competition from both new entrants and existing restaurants that have increased their digital presence through delivery and take-out platforms. We compete with delivery kitchens, food aggregators, and third-party delivery marketplaces such as DoorDash, Grubhub, and Uber Eats, as well as grocery stores that focus on freshly prepared or organic foods. The delivery marketplaces, including those we partner with, retain customer data for Sweetgreen orders and may use that information to promote other restaurants. The expansion of such delivery and take-out channels, especially among restaurants that previously relied on dine-in traffic, has further intensified overall competition in recent years.

Many competitors may have, among other things, greater financial and operational resources, lower costs, better geographic locations, better facilities, stronger management, more advanced technology, or more effective marketing. Some may imitate or improve upon our business model, menu, technology, or restaurant design, which are difficult to protect or not protectable under intellectual property or related laws, reducing our competitive advantages. Competitors may respond more quickly to shifts in consumer tastes, nutritional and dietary trends, and ordering preferences and may attract guests through lower prices, better loyalty or promotional programs, or broader menu offerings such as breakfast. Our sales could also decline due to changes in popular tastes or heightened attention to new restaurant concepts.

Any inability by us to compete effectively could reduce customer traffic, pressure our pricing, slow our growth, and prevent us from reaching profitability. We cannot make any assurances regarding our ability to effectively respond to consumer health perceptions or our ability to adapt our menu offerings to trends in eating habits. To achieve profitability, we have implemented cost-reduction initiatives and menu price increases since 2022 and may need to take similar actions in the future. Such measures could limit our ability to compete effectively on price or customer experience and could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Changes in economic conditions, macroeconomic and geopolitical events, and public health developments such as a pandemic may adversely affect customer behavior, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

paragraphs: You should read the following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations together with the audited consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this report. This discussion contains forward-looking statements based upon current plans, expectations, and beliefs that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those set forth in the sections titled "Risk Factors" and "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and in other parts of this report. Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this section to "we," "us," "our," the "Company," or "Sweetgreen" refer to Sweetgreen, Inc. and its subsidiaries.

Our fiscal year is a 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Sunday of the calendar year. Fiscal year 2025 was a 52-week period that ended December 28, 2025, fiscal year 2024 was a 52-week period that ended December 29, 2024, and fiscal year 2023 was a 53-week period that ended December 31, 2023. In a 52-week fiscal year, each fiscal quarter includes 13 weeks of operations. In a 53-week fiscal year, the first, second, and third fiscal quarters each include 13 weeks of operations, and the fourth fiscal quarter includes 14 weeks of operations.

A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 28, 2025, compared to the year ended December 29, 2024, is presented below. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 29, 2024, compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, can be found in Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 29, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 27, 2025.

We are a mission-driven, next generation restaurant and lifestyle brand that serves healthy food at scale. Our bold vision is to be as ubiquitous as traditional fast food, but with the transparency and quality that consumers increasingly expect. As of December 28, 2025, we owned and operated 281 restaurants in 24 states and Washington, D.C.

Opening new restaurants, including those with Infinite Kitchen technology, is an important driver of our revenue growth. In fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023, we had 35, 25, and 35 Net New Restaurant Openings. One of our strategies is to grow our footprint in both existing and new U.S. markets and, over time, internationally.

As of the end of fiscal year 2025, we utilized the Infinite Kitchen, a kitchen automation technology in 30 of our 281 restaurants. We incorporate the Infinite Kitchen technology into new and existing restaurants based, in large part, upon our evaluation of the potential economic and other benefits for those restaurants. We deployed units of the Infinite Kitchen in 18 of our new restaurants during fiscal year 2025 and 10 of our restaurants during fiscal year 2024. We continue to learn from these deployments and are incorporating our findings into future deployments.

As a premium offering in the fast-casual industry, we are exposed both to consumers trading the convenience of food away from home for the cost benefit of cooking, and to consumers selecting less expensive fast-casual alternatives during weaker economic periods. We have been impacted by a decrease in consumer spending during fiscal year 2025, which we expect to continue at least in the near term. As we focus on discipline with respect to costs and allocation of capital in connection with the Sweet Growth Transformation Plan, we will be opening fewer restaurants in the near term. In fiscal year 2026, we expect approximately 15 Net New Restaurant Openings, with about half featuring Infinite Kitchen units.

We have historically been able to partially offset rising costs - including inflation, tariffs, wage increases and increases in cost of goods sold - through gradual menu price increases, customer service and delivery fees, and operational efficiencies. There can be no assurance that we will be able to continue this practice in the current or future macroeconomic or regulatory environment. We also continue to see variability in our customer traffic patterns, including as a result of many workplaces adopting remote or hybrid models, which has shifted sales away from our In-Store Channel. Our Native Delivery, Outpost and Catering, and Marketplace Channels carry

higher costs due to third-party fees, elevated refund rates, and promotional activity, and a continued shift in sales mix toward these channels could pressure margins. However, we expect margins on these channels to improve over time as we achieve greater scale.

For fiscal year 2025, tariffs had minimal net impact on our average new unit development cost due to mitigation efforts including advance purchasing, strategic sourcing, and favorable trade policy changes. We expect to continue to be able to mitigate most of these costs in future periods.

For Infinite Kitchen units, the impact of tariffs in fiscal year 2025 was mitigated, in part, by our prepurchase of certain key materials. Tariffs increased the cost of Infinite Kitchen units by approximately 5% in fiscal year 2025. Going forward, we expect the cost of Infinite Kitchen units to modestly increase when taking into account the expected continuing impact of tariffs and additional amounts due to Wonder pursuant to our supply agreement with Wonder described below.

Management remains committed to mitigating the impact of tariff costs across our supply chain, restaurant build-outs and equipment through ongoing sourcing and cost-optimization strategies that we and our suppliers have implemented. Any future changes to the U.S. government's trade policies may impact these estimates.

On December 29, 2025, subsequent to fiscal year 2025 year end, we sold Spyce and certain assets relating to the Infinite Kitchen and other related kitchen automation technology and agreed to provide certain transition services to Wonder (such transaction, the "Spyce Sale"). At the time of the sale, we entered into a supply agreement and a license agreement in which Wonder has agreed to sell Infinite Kitchen units to us on a long-term basis and provide certain services related to the Infinite Kitchen units, including commissioning, support and maintenance.

Our revenue is derived from sales of food and beverage to customers through our five sales channels. We own and operate all of these channels other than our Marketplace Channel, which is operated by various third-party delivery marketplaces.

paragraphs: Sweetgreen, Inc., 一間設立於德國的公司（與其子公司合稱為 "Sweetgreen," "we,", "us," 或 "the Company"）為一項以使命為導向、新一代的餐廳與生活方式品牌，提供大量健康餐點。我們大膽的願景是成為如同傳統速食餐點一樣普遍，但擁有消費者日益期待的透明度與品質。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們在 24 個州與華盛頓特區擁有並營運 281 家餐廳。
我們設計的餐點為美味、可客製化且便利，以賦予消費者在午餐與晚餐時做出更健康的選擇。我們持續尋求方法來提升餐點，同時尊重我們的餐點理念。
我們的核心餐點為一組精心挑選的招牌餐點，全年無間斷地在所有分店提供，以確保一致的品質並反映我們的餐點哲學，並由嚴謹且可擴展的供應鏈支撐。顧客也可從廣泛的食材與招牌醬料中，自訂沙拉、碗裝或餐盤，使在標準化食材系統中實現有意義的客製化。
我們透過季節性與限定時限的餐點來補充核心餐點，使我們能引入新口味並測試創新，同時維持營運一致性。透過我們自有的數位通路，我們也提供獨家餐點與精選系列，以支持探索、個人化與顧客互動。
Sweetgreen 的使命是透過連結人們與真實食物，來建立更健康的社區。過去一年，我們的領導團隊已評估業務並重新調整戰略優先順序，以強化執行力、提升顧客體驗，並建立更穩健的財務模式。我們將此架構稱為 Sweet Growth Transformation Plan，其核心為五大戰略優先順序：
在所有餐廳內驅動一致的執行，以提供優質餐點、順暢營運與可靠的顧客體驗。
透過高品質食材與現做烹飪來區隔自己，同時持續以符合顧客期待的方式進化餐點。
透過針對性的數位互動、個人化訊息與相關優惠，來提升顧客造訪頻率與平均消費金額。
吸引新顧客透過強化 Sweetgreen 區別於其他品牌、具相關性且具文化吸引力的特色。
透過優先考量回報率、維持成本紀律並嚴謹配置資本，來實現可持續成長。
我們已建立一個差異化且完整的供應鏈，最終為顧客提供美味且高品質的食物。我們的採購與營運標準皆遵循 Sweetgreen Way，這是我們內部的價值觀，基於我們對原料品質、負責任採購及內製備餐的承諾。
我們與廣泛的國內食品夥伴網路合作，包括農民、製造商與經銷商。我們優先選擇符合我們標準且與我們食品哲學一致的原料，並與許多種植者及生產者維持直接關係。我們的供應鏈已組織成區域配送網路，並在與我們主要物流合作夥伴協商後進行管理，以促進一致性、可擴展性與營運可靠性。當我們進入新市場時，我們會尋求利用現有關係，同時維持這些標準。

在 Sweetgreen，我們將食品安全視為我們的「經營許可證」，這始於我們的食品供應。我們要求供應商在入夥流程中提供適當的食品安全認證。入夥後，我們會與供應商合作，確保其符合我們的產品品質規格。我們也遵循一項全面食品安全計畫（"CFSP"），其中包括核准供應商計畫、危害分析與關鍵控制點計畫、餐廳設計、施工與維護指南、新產品商業化流程，以及危機管理。根據我們的 CFSP，我們為餐廳設定了「sweet clean 標準」，這是用來指導營運者確保我們在食品安全與清潔方面的做法在所有餐廳中保持一致且可擴展。食品安全是我們現場領導者獎金計畫的重要組成部分；營運者除非達到相關期間的食品安全門檻，否則不會獲得某些獎金。除了我們的 CFSP 之外，我們還有一套驗證、稽核與監測系統，以確保我們的食品安全不會受到影響。
我們在財務年度 2025 年與 2024 年分別開設了 35 家與 25 家新餐廳，截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們總計擁有 281 家餐廳，分佈於 24 個州與華盛頓特區。我們預期在 2026 年開設的新餐廳數量將少於 2025 年。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之分析，並與本報告中其他處所載之審計合併財務報表及相關附註一併參考。本討論包含基於目前計畫、預期及信念之向前看陳述，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。我們實際結果可能與這些向前看陳述所預期者有重大差異，原因在於多種因素，包括於「風險因素」及「向前看陳述特別說明」等標題之節中所列舉者，以及其他本報告之部分。除非文意另有要求，否則本節所有提及「我們」、「我們」、「我們」、「公司」或「Sweetgreen」之參考，均指 Sweetgreen, Inc. 及其子公司。

我們的會計年度為 52 或 53 週之期間，並於歷年曆年最後一個星期日結束。會計年度 2025 為 52 週期間，於 2025 年 12 月 28 日結束，會計年度 2024 為 52 週期間，於 2024 年 12 月 29 日結束，會計年度 2023 為 53 週期間，於 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束。在 52 週會計年度中，每個會計季節包含 13 週營運。在 53 週會計年度中，第一、第二及第三會計季節各包含 13 週營運，而第四會計季節則包含 14 週營運。

關於截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日之年度，與截至 2024 年 12 月 29 日之年度之財務狀況及營運成果之討論，請見下列。關於截至 2024 年 12 月 29 日之年度，與截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日之年度之財務狀況及營運成果之討論，請參見我們於 2024 年 12 月 29 日結束之年度，於 2025 年 2 月 27 日提交至 SEC 之 10-K 年度報告中之第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之分析」。
我們為一個以使命為導向、新一代的餐廳與生活方式品牌，提供大規模的健康餐點。我們大膽的願景是成為如同傳統速食餐點一樣普遍，但具有消費者日益期待的透明度與品質。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們擁有並營運 281 家餐廳，分佈於 24 個州及華盛頓特區。
開設新餐廳，包括採用 Infinite Kitchen 技術之餐廳，是我們營收成長的重要驅動因素。在會計年度 2025、2024 及 2023，我們分別有 35、25 及 35 家新餐廳開幕。我們的策略之一是擴展我們在現有及新美國市場的據點，並在長遠之際，拓展國際市場。

截至會計年度 2025 結束，我們在 281 家餐廳中，有 30 家採用了 Infinite Kitchen，這是一種廚房自動化技術。我們根據對這些餐廳潛在經濟及其他效益之評估，將 Infinite Kitchen 技術應用於新舊餐廳。在會計年度 2025，我們在 18 家新餐廳部署了 Infinite Kitchen 單元，在會計年度 2024，我們在 10 家餐廳部署了 Infinite Kitchen 單元。我們持續從這些部署中學習，並將所獲得的經驗應用於未來的部署。

作為快閃餐飲產業中的高階選擇，我們同時面臨消費者將外食的便利性轉換為在家烹飪的經濟效益，以及在經濟較差時期，消費者選擇較便宜的快閃餐飲替代方案。我們在會計年度 2025 面臨消費者支出減少的影響，我們預期至少在近期內會持續。在執行 Sweet Growth Transformation Plan 的同時，我們將更加註重成本控制及資本配置，因此在近期內將減少開設新餐廳。在會計年度 2026，我們預期有約 15 家新餐廳開幕，其中約一半會採用 Infinite Kitchen 單元。
我們歷來能夠透過逐步提高餐點價格、顧客服務及配送費用，以及營運效率，部分抵消成本上升的影響，包括通貨膨脹、關稅、工資增加及商品成本增加。無法保證我們將能在目前或未來的總體經濟或法規環境中持續這種做法。我們也持續觀察到顧客流量的變動，包括因許多工作場所採用遠距或混合模式，導致銷售額從我們的門市通路轉移。我們的原生配送、Outpost 及婚宴、以及市場通路
較高的成本由於第三方費用、提高的退款率及促銷活動，以及銷售組合持續向這些通路轉移，可能會壓縮毛利率。然而，我們預期這些通路的毛利率會隨時間推移而改善，因為我們將達到更大的規模。
在財務年度 2025 年，關稅對我們平均新產品開發成本的淨影響極小，這是因為我們採取了包括預購、戰略採購及有利貿易政策變動等緩衝措施。我們預期未來期間仍能緩衝這些成本的大多數部分。
對於 Infinite Kitchen 單位，財務年度 2025 年的關稅影響部分被我們預購某些關鍵材料所緩衝。關稅使 Infinite Kitchen 單位的成本在財務年度 2025 年增加了約 5%。展望未來，我們預期 Infinite Kitchen 單位的成本會小幅上升，這已考慮到關稅持續影響的預期以及根據我們與 Wonder 的供應協議中所規定的額外金額。
管理階層仍致力於透過我們與供應商所實施的持續採購及成本優化策略，來緩衝供應鏈、餐廳裝修及設備的關稅成本影響。未來美國政府貿易政策的任何變動可能會影響這些預估。

於 2025 年 12 月 29 日，財務年度 2025 年結算後，我們出售了 Spyce 以及與 Infinite Kitchen 及其他相關廚房自動化技術有關的某些資產，並同意為 Wonder 提供某些過渡服務（此交易稱為 "Spyce Sale"）。在出售時，我們與 Wonder 籤訂了供應協議及授權協議，Wonder 同意以長期方式向我們銷售 Infinite Kitchen 單位，並提供與 Infinite Kitchen 單位相關的某些服務，包括啟動、支援及維護。
我們的營業收入來自透過我們五個銷售通路向客戶銷售食品及飲料。我們擁有並營運這些通路，除了 Marketplace Channel，該通路由各第三方配送市場平台所營運。

headings: 與本公司業務、品牌及產業相關之風險
我們所處的產業為高度競爭性產業。若我們無法有效競爭，將對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
嚴峻天氣條件及天然災害已對本公司餐廳銷售額及營運成果產生不利影響，氣候變遷可能進一步加劇這些不利影響。
自設立以來，本公司已產生顯著的淨虧損。我們預期在可預見的未來，淨虧損情況仍會持續，且本公司可能無法實現盈利。
本公司可能無法說服消費者願意為更高品質的食物支付我們的價格。
本公司未來的成長大幅依賴於本公司開設新餐廳的能力，且受到許多不可預測因素的影響。
本公司長期的成功高度依賴於本公司有效識別並取得適當場地以開設新餐廳的能力。
本公司擴張至新市場可能帶來更高的風險，並對本公司成長及營運成果產生不利影響。
新開設的餐廳，一旦開始營運，可能無法獲利，且新開設的餐廳可能對我們現有餐廳的銷售額產生負面影響。
食品安全及食源性疾病相關問題可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
若我們無法聘僱、培訓、獎勵並留住合適的員工，將可能對我們的成長與獲利能力產生不利影響。
勞動成本增加、勞動力短缺或工會化運動可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
食品及供應成本的變動或原料及其他供應品的可得性或配送中斷，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們對第三方的依賴可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
若無法有效管理我們的成長，可能損害我們的業務及營運成果。
商品及其他營運成本的變動，特別是因氣候變遷所致，可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
未能維持本公司企業文化，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司行銷策略與通路將持續演進，且本公司方案可能無法成功。
paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，並配合本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析部分，以及合併財務報表與相關附註。若下列所描述的風險與不確定性實際發生或持續發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果，以及本公司A類普通股之交易價格造成重大且不利的影響。下列所描述的風險與不確定性為本公司已識別為重大者，但並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險與不確定性。本公司業務亦受一般性風險與不確定性影響，這些風險與不確定性可能影響許多其他公司，包括但不限於總體經濟與產業條件，以及目前尚未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要，但未來可能出現或變得重要，並可能對本公司業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運成果或本公司A類普通股之交易價格造成負面影響。

本公司面臨來自快餐速食與傳統速食餐廳業態的激烈競爭。這些業態競爭因素包括風味、價格、食物品質與呈現方式、服務、位置與餐廳環境。本公司競爭對手包括當地經營的餐廳與區域性及全國性連鎖餐廳，提供堂食、外帶、外送與婚宴服務。許多競爭對手經營時間較長，市場佔有率較為成熟，擁有遠較本公司為多的財務、行銷、人力及其他資源，因此可能在高度競爭的餐廳產業中更具優勢。本公司競爭對手包括全國性與區域性快餐速食連鎖餐廳、強調潔淨食材與健康飲食的餐廳，以及傳統速食餐廳。

隨著本公司持續擴張至新市場並進一步發展數位通路，同時也面臨來自新進企業與已營運餐廳的競爭，這些餐廳透過外送與外帶平台增加其數位存在。本公司與外送廚房、食品聚合商及第三方外送平台如DoorDash、Grubhub與Uber Eats競爭，同時也與專注於新鮮製備或有機食品的超市競爭。外送平台，包括本公司合作的平台，會保留Sweetgreen訂單的客戶資料，並可能利用這些資訊來推廣其他餐廳。外送與外帶通路的擴張，特別是那些原本依賴堂食客流量的餐廳，已進一步加劇整體競爭，尤其在近年來更加明顯。

許多競爭對手可能擁有較多的財務與運營資源、較低的成本、較佳的地理位置、較佳的設施、較強的管理團隊、較先進的科技或較有效的行銷策略。有些競爭對手可能模仿或改進我們的商業模式、餐點、科技或餐廳設計，這些都難以保護或無法透過智慧財產權或其他相關法律保護，從而降低我們的競爭優勢。競爭對手可能更快適應消費者口味的變化、營養與飲食趨勢的改變，以及訂購偏好，並透過較低的價格、更好的忠誠度或促銷活動，或更廣泛的餐點選擇（如早餐）來吸引顧客。我們的銷售額也可能因消費者口味的改變或對新餐廳概念的關注而下降。
若本公司無法有效競爭，將導致顧客流量減少、壓縮我們的價格、延緩我們的成長，並使我們無法達成獲利。本公司無法保證我們能有效回應消費者對健康的觀感，或能適應飲食習慣的趨勢。為達成獲利，本公司自2022年起已實施成本削減措施與餐點價格調漲，未來可能也需要採取類似行動。這些措施可能限制我們在價格或顧客體驗上的競爭能力，並對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成負面影響。
經濟條件的變化、總體經濟與地緣政治事件，以及公共衛生發展（如疫情）可能影響消費者行為，進而對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成負面影響。
